record.paper_title: Some open problems in the theory of almost periodic functions
record.context_brief: Nature of elements of APr for 1<r<2
record.original_question: For intermediate exponents 1<r<2, determine what kind of mathematical objects the elements of APr(R, C) are. In particular, clarify whether an element of APr should be represented by an actual function, by an equivalence class of functions, or by some other type of object, given that AP1 consists of functions while AP2=B2 consists of equivalence classes.

evidence.quote:
b) What can we say about the nature of elements of the spaces APr, r ∈ (1; 2)?
For r = 1 they are functions, but for r = 2 they are classes of equivalent functions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a real number $r \ge 1$, let $AP_r(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C})$ denote the Besicovitch-type space of almost periodic functions defined as follows. A trigonometric polynomial is a finite sum $P(t)=\sum_{k=1}^{N} a_k e^{i\lambda_k t}$ with $a_k\in\mathbb{C}$ and $\lambda_k\in\mathbb{R}$. On the linear space of trigonometric polynomials consider the seminorm 
$$\|f\|_{r} \;=\; \left(\limsup_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{2T}\int_{-T}^{T}|f(t)|^{r}\,dt\right)^{1/r}.$$
Define $AP_r(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C})$ to be the completion of the space of trigonometric polynomials with respect to $\|\cdot\|_r$. 

It is known that:
(i) for $r=1$, the elements of $AP_1$ may be realized as honest pointwise-defined functions $\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{C}$;
(ii) for $r=2$, the space $AP_2$ coincides with the Besicovitch space $B^2$, whose elements are equivalence classes of measurable functions modulo functions with vanishing quadratic mean.

Determine the precise nature of the elements of $AP_r(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C})$ for intermediate exponents $1<r<2$: can each element be canonically represented by an actual function $\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{C}$, must it be regarded as an equivalence class of measurable functions modulo a suitable null subspace, or is some other description required?
artifact.status_search_result: Standard references describe $AP_1$/$B^1$ and $AP_2 = B^2$ in the classical way (functions vs. equivalence classes), but no source located identifies a definitive characterization of the nature of elements of $AP_r$ for intermediate $1<r<2$. The question is posed as an explicit open problem and no resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: Almost periodic function - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The space Bp of Besicovitch almost periodic functions ... contains the space Wp of Weyl almost periodic functions. If one quotients out a subspace of 'null' functions, it can be identified with the space of Lp functions on the Bohr compactification.
status_evidence.claim: Standard description treats Bp elements as equivalence classes after quotienting null functions, without distinguishing the intermediate-exponent case.

status_evidence.title: Almost-periodic function - Encyclopedia of Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: Encyclopedia entry on classes of almost periodic functions in the sense of Besicovitch, Weyl, Stepanov.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference does not single out a resolution for 1<r<2.
